requirements.title: gpux-zed-util spawns and reaps macOS child processes without async-process's git fork

criteria.descriptionMarkdown: No source under `crates/` calls `adopt_raw_pid(`. `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` contain no `[patch` section and no `source = "git+` dependency. The macOS `Child` in `darwin.rs` is backed by a gpux-owned process handle, and `gpux-zed-util` compiles on macOS with all its test targets.

A new, separately selectable test group for the process handle (the `command::darwin::process` tests) proves on macOS:

**Status and output**
- `status()` and `output()` return the child's real exit status.
- Two concurrent `status()` futures and a later `try_status()` all observe the same exit status.

**Kill**
- `try_status()` returns `None` while the child runs.
- `kill()` ends a running child with `SIGKILL` and is still a successful no-op after the child was reaped.

**Reaping**
- A dropped `Child` whose process has exited, or exits later, is reaped: `kill(pid, 0)` reports `ESRCH` within 10 s, so no zombie is left.
- `kill_on_drop(true)` kills and reaps a running child.
- A stress test spawns at least 50 short-lived children with distinct exit codes, mixing concurrent `status()` futures, `try_status()` polling and drops. Every child is reaped exactly once with its own exit code. No call may observe a reaped-twice `ECHILD` as an error while a status is cached.

The tests must fail, not skip, if spawning fails.

The existing `command::darwin::tests` group, which has never compiled in gpux before, passes on macOS unchanged. It covers pipes not inherited by unrelated spawns, drop reaping, kill-on-drop, echo/cat/stderr/exit-code/current-dir/env/status spawns, env removal and clearing, null and piped stdio, and bare-program PATH resolution. The replacement must not weaken or delete any of these tests.

requirements.title: The whole gpux workspace builds on macOS exactly as CI checks it

criteria.descriptionMarkdown: On macOS, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` exits 0 at the Gpux root, matching CI's macOS step exactly. This includes the `gpux-apple` build script compiling `shaders.metal` with the real `xcrun metal` and `metallib`. It must not get there by excluding crates or targets, by cfg-gating code away from macOS without equivalent behavior, or by adding git dependencies or `[patch]` sections.
`cargo check -p gpux-apple --all-targets --features runtime_shaders` passes on macOS. This build embeds the stitched `scene.h` + `shaders.metal` source instead of a prebuilt metallib.

`cargo check -p gpux-apple --all-targets --target aarch64-apple-ios` passes on macOS, compiling the shaders against the iOS SDK through the build script's `iphoneos` branch. Prerequisite: `rustup target add aarch64-apple-ios` and Xcode's iOS SDK.

requirements.title: The Metal renderer's premultiplied paint contract is proven on macOS

criteria.descriptionMarkdown: On macOS, `cargo test -p gpux-apple --lib paint_packing` passes. The existing `paint_packing_*` tests prove that a solid background packs its `PaintColor` unchanged and that prepared gradient stops are appended with their prepared colors, offsets and color space.

A new, separately selectable test group, `metal_paint_contract`, renders scenes through the headless Metal renderer (`MetalRenderer::new_headless` / `MetalHeadlessRenderer`) and asserts read-back pixels. Each case uses exact geometry and colors. The tests must fail, not skip, when no Metal device is available.

- **Translucent fill.** White at 4.5% alpha over `#0a0a0a` reads `#151515` (±1 per channel), the encoded-sRGB composite.
- **Dashed borders.** A 200×56 box with a 4 px dashed border, where gaps fall at x ≡ 8–12 mod 12 px. With no fill and a white border over `#0a0a0a`, gap centres read the backdrop (±1) and dash centres read white. With a `#404040` fill and a `#0e7490` border, gap centres read the fill and no top-border pixel is brighter than the brighter of fill and border.
- **Premultiplied gradient interpolation.** An sRGB linear gradient from opaque red to fully transparent blue, over black, reads about (128, 0, 0) ±3 at its midpoint with blue ≤ 3.
- **OKLab gradient.** An OKLab gradient from opaque red to opaque blue reads, at its midpoint, the encoded-sRGB value that `gpux_color` computes for the same OKLab interpolation (±3, allowing for dither).
- **Inset versus drop shadow.** An inset shadow with blur 0 paints the band between its element bounds and its hole in the shadow color, leaves the hole and everything outside the element at the backdrop, and the same shadow as a drop shadow does the opposite.
- **Alpha on a transparent target.** With the renderer set transparent (`update_transparency(true)`, clear alpha 0), two overlapping 50% black quads leave alpha 0.75 (±1/255) in their overlap: source-over, not saturating accumulation.
The `metal_paint_contract` group also passes with `--features runtime_shaders`. That proves the stitched source compiles at runtime through `new_library_with_source` and renders identically.
`cargo clippy -p gpux-apple --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` passes on macOS. CI lints only on Windows, where this code is compiled out.

**Native visual proof in RayX's Test Suite.** From `../RayX`, run `cargo run -p xtask -- app apps/test_suite run macos --no-default-features --features rayx_diagnostics,devkit` and inspect it through the `rayx-devkit-mcp` sidecar (RayX `.claude/skills/rayx/references/diagnostics.md`). Each page must render like the same page on headed WebGPU on the same Mac.

**Pages:**
- `/rendering/srgb-compositing`: translucent colors equal the values `rayx-srgb-compositing.spec.ts` encodes.
- `/rendering/border-antialiasing`: 1 px rounded rings do not bead and thick borders stay solid. This closes the memory rule that the Metal border-antialiasing port is not done until it passes on macOS.
- `/rendering/dashed-borders`: gaps show the backdrop or fill.
- Pages showing sRGB and OKLab gradients, drop and inset shadows, text, SVG icons, images and color emoji.

**Hardware double-checks:**
- Emoji and image edges show no dark or bright fringes. This validates the straight-alpha polychrome atlas assumption; if it fails, inspect what `gpui_macos` uploads.
- Text weight and contrast match macOS expectations. Monochrome sprites ignore `MonochromeSpriteKind` and get no gamma correction on Metal.
- A transparent window composites correctly, if Test Suite offers one; otherwise record that none exists.

**Crash smoke:** opening every listed page produces no panic or Metal validation error in the logs.

Any shader or renderer defect found here is repaired in `crates/gpui_apple` and re-proven by PAINT-2.

states: gradient, shadow, text, icon, image and emoji pages
visual.viewport: Native macOS Test Suite window on the Mac's built-in Retina display (DPR 2), compared with headed WebGPU Chromium on the same machine
visual.descriptionMarkdown: Compare each Metal-rendered page with its WebGPU rendering, using DevKit/MCP screenshots stored under `artifacts-temp/agentx/macos-only-metal-port-and-ci-repair/`. Colors and coverage must match within visual tolerance, and nothing may be missing, doubled, fringed or wrongly blended.

requirements.title: The WGPU dashed-border fix lands with its paired RayX proof
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Since cb4130b, `fs_quad` in `crates/gpui_wgpu/src/shaders.wgsl` faded dashed borders through alpha alone. Gaps therefore added the premultiplied border color onto the fill or backdrop, and dashed borders rendered nearly solid on every WGPU backend; RayX chart tooltips use them. Gpux `c6b6512` scales the whole premultiplied color and adds a shader-source regression test; `e7149e7` records the rule in memory. RayX `f1a9be7b` adds `/rendering/dashed-borders` and `rayx-dashed-borders.spec.ts`. On Windows the spec failed 4/4 before the fix and passed 4/4 after it.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown: The integration branch contains `c6b6512` and `e7149e7`, brought in by merging `fix/wgpu-dashed-border-gaps` (merge, no rebase or cherry-pick rewrite). `cargo test -p gpux-wgpu-renderer --lib dashed_border` passes on macOS.

On the Mac, with Gpux on the integration branch and RayX on `test/dashed-border-gaps`, `rayx-dashed-borders.spec.ts` passes all 4 runs: headed WebGPU and forced WebGL2, at DPR 1 and 2. This proves the fix on Chromium's macOS backends.

requirements.title: The upstream Windows grandchild-process test stops timing out on loaded runners
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: `crates/util/src/process.rs`, `windows_tests::spawn_process_tree`, comes from upstream Zed and is unchanged in gpux. It waits only 5 s for a cold `powershell.exe` to start `ping.exe` and write a pid file. On PR #2 (WGSL-only changes) it timed out once in `test (windows)`, and the re-run passed. Upstream `main` still uses 5 s.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
The pid-file deadline in `spawn_process_tree` is raised from 5 s to 30 s, keeping the 50 ms poll and the same process tree, so the behavior under test (job-object termination of grandchildren) is unchanged. The change is recorded as a gpux patch in the import guide (DOCS-2).

Verification is manual: a reviewer confirms the diff, which touches only the test helper's deadline. CI's `test (windows)` job then passes on the published PR (PUB-1). The test is `#[cfg(all(test, windows))]` and cannot compile or run on macOS.

requirements.title: Durable knowledge reflects the proven macOS state
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: gpux memory still records the Metal paint-contract and border-antialiasing ports as never compiled or run. It also places the Metal renderer in `gpui_macos`, although it now lives in `gpui_apple`. The import guide's patch-surface list has no Metal or macOS process entries, so the next Zed import could bring back upstream's `Hsla` shaders or the fork-only `adopt_raw_pid` call.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**gpux memory matches what this epic proved.**
- `platform/desktop` state, knowledge, rules and hypotheses: the Metal renderer in `gpui_apple` consumes premultiplied encoded-sRGB `PaintColor` and blends premultiplied. Its border-antialiasing port is proven or not, per PAINT-5; settle the hypothesis and rule accordingly. macOS child processes are reaped by `darwin/process.rs`.
- `renderer/state.md` names `gpui_apple`.
- A knowledge item: Metal-exported enums must be `#[repr(C)]`, because cbindgen writes a sized enum as a separate C typedef that Metal's C++ rejects as a redefinition.
- The trade-off text of `.agentx/memory/decisions/renderer/wgpu/2026-09-30-renderer-wgpu-srgb-compositing.md` no longer calls the Metal port unproven.
- Epic-end promotion candidates are handled per the `context --epic` promotion packet.

`python3 <installed agentx>/scripts/audit_agentx_memory.py` reports the memory structure consistent. No raw logs go into memory.

**`.claude/skills/gpux/references/update-from-zed-gpui-closure.md` records three replay rules**, each with why upstream's version must not be taken wholesale:
- The Metal renderer consumes premultiplied `PaintColor`. cbindgen parses `gpux_color`'s `paint.rs`. Metal-exported enums stay `repr(C)`. Upstream's `shaders.metal` still uses `Hsla`.
- Upstream `darwin.rs` calls the fork-only `adopt_raw_pid`; gpux replaces it with `darwin/process.rs`.
- The Windows `spawn_process_tree` deadline is a gpux patch.

`ToFix/` is removed once every note it holds is carried by commits, this epic or memory.

requirements.title: The work is published for review with every CI job green
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: The earlier pull requests (rayx-ui/Gpux#1, #2 and rayx-ui/RayX#1) were closed unmerged, and their branches were kept. CI runs on pull requests and on pushes to `main`.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
With the user's explicit approval at that moment:
- The integration branch is pushed and a Gpux PR is opened against `main`. Its description covers all four notes and references the closed PRs, and it lists the exact validation and anything unverified.
- All five CI jobs are green on that PR: `check (ubuntu-latest)`, `check (windows-latest)`, `check (macos-latest)`, `test (windows)` and `package`.
- The paired RayX PR from `test/dashed-border-gaps` is opened or updated against `master`. It references the Gpux PR and must be merged together with it or after it, because the dashed-borders spec fails against a Gpux checkout without `c6b6512`.

No merge happens in this epic.
